question: I'm a sociology major going into my junior year soon, what are all the courses I still need to take for the major besides the intro ones?
answer:
The catalog lists the following Sociology BA major requirements besides SOCI 101 INTRODUCTION TO SOCIOLOGY. It can’t show which you personally still need without your records. [1]

Required courses: SOCI 202 SOCIAL INEQUALITY; SOCI 215 SOCIOLOGY OF RACE RELATIONS; SOCI 250 INTERNATIONAL MIGRATION & HUMAN RIGHTS; SOCI 302 WOMEN AND GLOBAL POVERTY or SOCI 361 GENDER, WORK, AND FAMILY; SOCI 304 GLOBALIZATION AND SOCIETY; SOCI 307 SOCIAL RESEARCH WITH COMPUTERS; SOCI 308 DATA ANALYSIS IN SOCIOLOGY; SOCI 317 SOCIOLOGY OF COMMUNITY: FIELDWORK; SOCI 332 SOCIAL THEORY; SOCI 410 CAPSTONE PROJECT IN SOCIOLOGY. [1]

Concentration requirements: Criminology requires SOCI 245 CRIMINOLOGY and at least 2 electives from SOCI 248 CRIME AND MEDIA; SOCI 255 HUMAN RIGHTS IN THE CONTEXT OF LAW ENFORCEMENT; SOCI 315 SOCIOLOGY OF DEVIANCE; SOCI 345 RACE, CRIME AND JUSTICE; SOCI 390 TOPICS. Social Inequality requires at least 3 electives from ANTH 220 FOOD AND CULTURE; ANTH 238 URBAN ANTHROPOLOGY; ANTH 314 CROSSING BORDERS: GROWING UP LATINX; an unnamed catalog entry; SOCI 203 SOCIOLOGY OF SPORT; SOCI 205 SOCIOLOGY OF AGING; SOCI 206 ENVIRONMENTAL SOCIOLOGY; SOCI 221 SOCIAL MOVEMENTS; SOCI 230 SOCIOLOGY OF HEALTH & MEDICINE; SOCI 232 SOCIOLOGY OF FAMILY; SOCI 260 SOCIOLOGY OF MEDIA AND POP CULTURE; SOCI 303 SOCIOLOGY OF CULTURE; SOCI 309 FOOD AND POPULATION; SOCI 331 SOCIOLOGY OF RELIGION; SOCI 335 PUBLIC SOCIOLOGIES. [1]

Career Pathways also requires PATH 001 CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 1, PATH 002 CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 2, and PATH 003 CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 3. [1]

To identify what remains for you, review your Degree Audit (https://web.ramapo.edu/degree-audit-tools/) and make an appointment with your faculty academic advisor; see the scheduling slides if needed: https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/wp-content/uploads/sites/133/2026/02/How-to-Schedule-an-Appointment.pdf. [10]
Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): success@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7441. [10]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-BA-SOCI) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/)
note_A: Sociology BA groups match exactly: Major Requirements (SOCI 202, 215, 250, 302 or 361, 304, 307, 308, 317, 332, 410 besides SOCI 101), Criminology concentration (SOCI 245 + at least 2 of 248/255/315/345/390), Social Inequality (at least 3 of the listed ANTH/SOCI courses plus one unnamed entry), and Career Pathways PATH 001-003. SOSC 235 appears only as School Core in older-cohort plans, and the Provost CAP page says School Core is no longer a graduation requirement, so leaving it out is fine.
note_B: Checked Sociology BA requirement groups: required list (SOCI 202, 215, 250, 302 or 361, 304, 307, 308, 317, 332, 410), Criminology (SOCI 245 + at least 2 of 248/255/315/345/390), Social Inequality (at least 3 of the listed ANTH/SOCI electives incl. an unnamed entry) and PATH 001-003 all match the data and course names; declining personal progress is fine.

question: how many credits do i need total to graduate from ramapo
answer:
For an undergraduate degree, you need at least 128 credits to graduate [1][2][3][6][9]. Some programs may require more [6][8], and program requirements differ, so review the credits with your adviser [3]. At least 48 credits at Ramapo, including your final 32 in residence, are stated on the Registrar’s graduation page [1]; the FAQ and Catalog instead say at least 32 credits at Ramapo [2][3][6]. These pages differ. Contact the Registrar at reg@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7695, D-224, to ask about your requirements [1][2][3].

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/) [6](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#graduation-requirements) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/faqs/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/policies/)
note_A: 128 credits is stated on the Registrar FAQ, the graduation page, the catalog Graduation Requirements and Student Success policies. The graduation page does say a minimum of 48 at Ramapo with the final 32 in residence, while the FAQ and catalog say a minimum of 32, so the discrepancy is reported accurately. Registrar contacts match.
note_B: 128 credits appears on the Registrar FAQ, graduation page, catalog graduation requirements and Student Success policies; the 48-credit/final-32 (Registrar graduation page) vs 32-credit (FAQ, catalog) difference is real in the data; Registrar contact (reg@ramapo.edu, 684-7695, D-224) matches.

question: can one class count for both my major and a minor at the same time or do they have to be separate?
answer:
Yes. Courses fulfilling your primary or secondary major may also count toward your minor, but no more than half of the credits required in the minor may overlap. [1]

The Office of the Provost publishes this rule: [1] https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1
Email provost@ramapo.edu or call (201) 684-7330. The office is on the first floor of the Birch Mansion.

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1)
note_A: Catalog Integrity of Degree Programs: courses fulfilling the primary or secondary major may count toward the minor but may not exceed one-half of the credits required in the minor. The Provost phone (201) 684-7330, provost@ email and Birch Mansion first floor all appear on the Provost page.
note_B: Catalog Integrity of Degree Programs: courses for the primary or secondary major may count toward the minor but may not exceed one-half of the minor's credits; Provost contact (provost@ramapo.edu, 684-7330, first floor Birch Mansion) is on the Provost pages.

question: what are the prereqs for the research methods course in psych, and do i need stats done first?
answer:
PSYC 303 Research Methods in Psychology is 4 credits. Its prerequisites are all of: CRWT 102 Critical Reading and Writing II or CRWT 102S Critical Reading and Writing II; PSYC 101 Introduction to Psychology; and PSYC 242 Statistics or BADM 225 Management Statistics [2].

Yes—statistics must be completed first, through PSYC 242 or the listed alternative BADM 225. PSYC 242 is itself 4 credits and requires one of: MATH 100T Transfer GE Math Equivalent, MATH 101 Math with Applications, MATH 104 Math for the Modern World, MATH 106 Introduction to Mathematical Modeling, MATH 108 Elementary Probability and Statistics, MATH 110 Precalculus, or MATH 121 Calculus I [3].

The Psychology BA lists PSYC 242 and PSYC 303 as required major courses [1].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-BA-PSYC) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PSYC303) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PSYC242)
note_A: courses.json: PSYC 303 is 4 credits, prerequisites all of CRWT 102/102S, PSYC 101 and PSYC 242 or BADM 225. PSYC 242 is 4 credits with any of MATH 100T/101/104/106/108/110/121. Psychology BA Major Requirements include PSYC 242 and PSYC 303.

question: What gen ed requirements are there overall at Ramapo? I'm trying to figure out which categories I still have left to fill.
answer:
Ramapo’s published curriculum describes ten General Education courses [13]:
1. Four keystone courses: First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102, and Studies in the Arts & Humanities. Critical Reading & Writing 102 must be taken within the first 64 credits [13].
2. One course in each of four keystone categories: Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning. Quantitative Reasoning must be taken within the first 64 credits [13].
3. One course in two of three distribution categories: Culture & Creativity, Systems, Sustainability, & Society, and Values & Ethics. At least one distribution course must be offered by a school other than the school housing your major [13].
The catalog also lists the required courses as First-Year Seminar, Critical Reading and Writing II, Social Science Inquiry, and Studies in the Arts and Humanities, plus the four keystone categories and two distribution categories [1, 3]. It says reading/writing and mathematics must be completed by 64 credits; Banner can block schedule creation or adjustment if the requirements are unmet at that point [7, 8].
The distribution-category name differs across pages: section 6 calls one category “Social Systems and Society,” while sections 1 and 13 call it “Systems, Sustainability, and Society” [1, 6, 13]. Section 6 says choose two of the three categories; beginning Fall 2026, the “out of school requirement” is no longer enforced in degree audit tools [6].
I can’t verify which categories you personally still need. Review your Degree Audit, then make an appointment with your faculty academic advisor [9]: https://web.ramapo.edu/degree-audit-tools/. For help, contact the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising) at success@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7441, D-207.

Sources: [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/)
note_A: Matches the Provost Curriculum page (4 keystone courses, 4 keystone categories, 2 of 3 distribution categories, CRWT 102 and QR within 64 credits, out-of-school rule), the catalog General Education policy and the Banner 64-credit block. The CAP resources page does say 'Social Systems and Society' and that the out-of-school requirement is not enforced from Fall 2026. Restating the list twice and discussing section numbers adds clutter.
note_B: Provost curriculum page gives ten courses: four keystone courses, four keystone categories, two of three distribution categories with the out-of-school rule and 64-credit timing; CAP resources page gives the 'Social Systems and Society' name and says the out-of-school rule is not enforced from Fall 2026; catalog Reading/Writing/Math section describes the Banner block; Student Success contact D-207 matches.

question: is there a capstone or senior seminar for political science majors and what year are you supposed to take it?
answer:

question: I'm thinking about adding a minor in economics as a soc major. What classes are in the econ minor and are any of them upper level?

question: how many credits is psyc 101 and what does it actually cover
answer:
PSYC 101 INTRODUCTION TO PSYCHOLOGY is 4 credits [1]. It introduces psychology as a field of study and practice, exploring its history, methods, and scope. Topics include learning, perception, cognition, emotion, motivation, abnormal behavior, psychotherapy, social behavior, personality, development across the lifespan, and the biological bases of thought, feeling, and action [1].

question: what are all the gen ed requirements i need to graduate, like how many categories are there
answer:
Ramapo students take ten General Education courses [3]: four keystone courses, one course in each of four keystone categories, and one course in two of three distribution categories [3].

- Keystone courses: First Year Seminar; Social Science Inquiry; Critical Reading & Writing 102 (within the first 64 credits); and Studies in the Arts & Humanities [3].
- Keystone categories: one course each in Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning. Quantitative Reasoning must be taken within the first 64 credits [3].
- Distribution categories: choose two of Culture & Creativity, Systems, Sustainability, & Society, and Values & Ethics. At least one course must be offered by a school other than the one housing your major [3].

So, there are four keystone categories and three distribution categories; you take courses in all four keystone categories and two of the three distribution categories [3]. The catalog describes the distribution choice as “Systems, Sustainability, and Society” [2]; section 1 instead calls it “Social Systems and Society.” The Provost page lists the three as Culture and Creativity, Values and Ethics, and Social Systems and Society, and says to select two [1].

Reading/writing and mathematics must be completed by 64 credit hours [9]. Transfer students may transfer or receive waivers for some or all requirements [8]; the listed waivers and remaining requirements for students with at least 48 credits are in section 4. See approved courses in the College Catalog: https://catalog.ramapo.edu/college-wide-programs/gened#general-education-categories-and-courses [5].

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [8](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education) [9](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education-reading-writing-and-mathematics)
note_A: Matches the Provost curriculum page: 10 courses, the 4 keystone courses, 4 keystone categories, 2 of 3 distribution categories, and CRWT 102 and QR by 64 credits. It states the out-of-school rule from the curriculum page without the newer note that it is no longer enforced from Fall 2026. The 'section 1' and 'section 4' references are clutter.
note_B: Ten courses, four keystone courses, four keystone categories, two of three distribution categories, 64-credit rules and transfer waivers all match the Provost curriculum page and catalog policies. But it states the out-of-school distribution rule as a requirement while the Provost CAP resources page it cites says that rule is no longer enforced in degree audit tools as of Fall 2026; it also has dangling 'section 1'/'section 4' references.
